prize_parts.citation: for the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules, either bifunctional degraders or molecular glues, redirect the ubiquitin-proteasome system to remove chosen proteins

statement.case_for: After the full round-1 exchange I keep B045 with Crews, Deshaies and Handa as a single part. The scientific core is unchanged and, I think, strengthened by the discussion: induced proximity makes ubiquitin-dependent proteolysis a designable chemical event, with ternary-complex structures, cooperativity and degradation kinetics as quantitative evidence, which is the kind of principle I can explain to a broad audience. It is also the only candidacy where six of eight members place it first or as an alternative, and the objections raised against it are about credit boundaries and clinical timing, not about whether the chemistry is real. Round 1 sharpened one point for me. Aili's observation that the glue branch is already clinically mature while the PROTAC branch is not argues for a citation that names both strands openly, so the committee states exactly what is rewarded: the concept of directed degradation (Crews, Deshaies) and the identification of cereblon as the target through which glues act (Handa). I would not describe this as one discovery; I would describe it as one principle reached by two independent routes, and the citation says so.
statement.case_against: The credit problem has not gone away. Ciulli (VHL ligands, ternary-complex structure), Gray, Sakamoto, Kim and Ito all have defensible claims, and a three-name cap forces a cut that colleagues can contest. My reasoning for the cut is that the Crews and Deshaies PROTAC concept and Handa's cereblon identification are different in kind, each opening a branch that the others then optimised, while Ciulli's and Gray's work, important as it is, is development of the concept and the ligase handles rather than the origin of either branch. That argument is judgment, not proof, and it is weakest for Ciulli. Maturity is the second weakness: no PROTAC is approved at scale, so the prize would lean on the concept and on the thalidomide-analogue clinical record. If the committee decides that a clinical verdict is required, B069 is the defensible fallback.

responses.point: Somfai holds B069 as the cleanest attribution and the longest record of confirmation, with ligand design as the unifying logic and a Buchwald and Hartwig pair needing no arbitrary cut.
responses.response: I accept that B069 is the best-attributed and most mature candidate on the list and I have kept it as my first alternative. What I still cannot see is a chemical addition that the committee could state as a new principle: the citation reads as a general method for a bond type within the field the 2010 prize already recognised, and both you and Zou list that overlap and the Kosugi and Migita chronology as unresolved. If five members decide that maturity and clean credit outweigh a new modality, I would vote for B069 without reservation, but I would ask you to say what the bulky-phosphine ligand design taught chemists about oxidative addition and reductive elimination that the C-C coupling work did not.

responses.point: Aili supports B045 but insists the citation say openly that it rewards the concept and cereblon rather than optimisation, and notes the glue branch is clinically mature while the PROTAC branch is not.
responses.response: I agree and have changed my wording accordingly: the round-2 citation names bifunctional degraders and molecular glues explicitly, so that Handa's place is explained by the cereblon mechanism and not by PROTAC development. Your maturity point also helps with the clinical objection, because the glue strand already has a clinical record that the PROTAC strand has not yet matched. I would still ask you whether you would accept Ciulli in place of Handa if the committee prefers a PROTAC-centred citation; my answer is no, because it would drop the strand with the strongest clinical evidence.

responses.point: Aqvist prefers B009 for Cullis, Anderson and Langer, arguing that the pKa-dependent ionizable lipid is a single design principle with global demonstrated consequences that complete the 2023 Medicine story.
responses.response: The pKa argument is the best version of the B009 case and it moves me from sceptical to genuinely interested; I have put B009 as my second alternative. My remaining difficulty is the credit boundary you concede yourself. Cullis, Hope, Madden and MacLachlan developed the Vancouver strand and Anderson and Langer the combinatorial and in vivo strand, so a Cullis, Anderson and Langer trio splits two groups, and I cannot yet name the single act of discovery. I would need a defensible reading in which Cullis stands for the principle and the other two for a separable achievement before I could place it above B045.

responses.point: Chabes ranks B045 first, treats degradation as a designable chemical reaction based on induced proximity, and keeps Handa over Ciulli because cereblon differs in kind from the PROTAC concept.
responses.response: I agree on both the framing and the Handa choice, and your wording on bifunctional degraders and glues is the basis of my citation. Your mention of B032 and B026 as fallbacks if B045 is judged early is a fair hedge; for me B069 is the better fallback because its credit is cleaner, while B026 would raise the Liu-only and Komor and Gaudelli question that the chair summary leaves open.

responses.point: Zou supports B069 for Buchwald and Hartwig on mechanistic evidence for the catalytic cycle, daily use in pharmaceutical process chemistry, and clean credit, and notes the 2010 prize covered C-C coupling only.
responses.response: The mechanistic evidence you cite (oxidative addition, amine binding, reductive elimination) is the strongest argument for B069 being more than ligand screening, and it is why I treat it as a serious alternative. I still weigh the 2010 overlap more heavily than you do. Your own suggestion of a two-part prize is the one I considered most carefully: pairing B045 with B069 would give three people for the first part and a single laureate for the second, which means choosing Buchwald or Hartwig arbitrarily. I reject that, and so I keep a single part.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept the three-name cut Crews, Deshaies, Handa against Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto, Kim and Ito; Ciulli's claim is the hardest to set aside.
Whether the absence of an approved PROTAC drug makes recognition premature compared with B069, whose maturity is not in doubt.
Whether a single citation covering bifunctional degraders and molecular glues credits one principle fairly or merges two achievements.
Whether the committee will value attribution cleanliness and maturity over novelty of capability; I do not claim support counts settle this.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict or recusal need to disclose on any shortlisted candidate. I am a physicist at Lund, with colleagues Somfai and Sparr also at Lund, but no candidate in my profile is linked to Lund and I have no personal or institutional tie to any credited name. My first-round alternative B018 is dropped because it had no support beyond my own opening ranking.
